thread:
maria.g: FYI customer acme-corp (private deployment in eu-west-1) reporting API auth timeouts and 502s since ~10:15 UTC. They say their on-prem firewall had a firmware update at 10:00 and tunnels started flapping. Can oncall join?
ankur: I'm looking. Any short traces or error patterns? TLS handshake failures or pure packet loss?
natalie: I can see a BGP flap on the Direct Connect VIF around 10:12 in our console, correlated with several control-plane TLS timeouts to the customer's control endpoint.
ops-oncall: Got ping. Checking IPsec/ike logs on our side now. If the firewall upgrade changed NAT or DF behavior, we may be seeing fragmented ESP packets dropped.
support-esc: Customer reports DNS resolution inside their VPC intermittently timing out too, affecting service discovery for the private API endpoints. They flagged these as P1.
infra-bot: Incident created: INC-2026-1892. Alerting network team.
ankur: Can we get customer-side tcpdump/pcap at their egress for packets to our control plane? Ask them to capture on the firewall for traffic to our IP range: `34.120.0.0/14` and ports UDP/500, UDP/4500, TCP/443.
maria.g: Requested pcaps from customer. They attached one; gist link: https://acme-pcaps.example/pcap1 (private).
ops-oncall: Quick look at pcap: I see repeated IKEv2 exchanges with no completion. Lots of fragmented ESP (protocol 50) with DF=1 and MSS 1500 on their side. That will break when NAT or firewall blocks fragments.
jamie: Also seeing `NO_ROUTE` errors in our edge logs at 10:13 for their session IDs — suggests transient route withdraw on the DX side. Could be a firewall doing asymmetric egress.
natalie: Customer's BGP neighbor shows `holdtime` drops. They confirmed firewall policy now blocks outbound UDP > 1024 by default after update. That would break NAT-T (UDP 4500) when using ephemeral ports.
ankur: Two-pronged: 1) immediate mitigation—ask customer to whitelist UDP/500, UDP/4500 to our control plane and allow ephemeral outbound UDP for NAT-T; 2) if fragments dropping, reduce MTU on the tunnel interfaces or enable MSS clamping.
support-esc: Customer applied an allowlist to permit UDP 500/4500 and reopened ephemeral UDP. They still report intermittent DNS failures.
ops-oncall: DNS failures could be due to control-plane TLS handshakes failing and our side closing resolver connections. Can you `dig @10.0.0.2 api.internal.acme -p 53 +trace` on a healthy vs affected host and share outputs?
maria.g: Pasted diffs: healthy host shows replies in <20ms. Affected host shows no response until TCP fallback, then timeouts.
jamie: That suggests firewall is treating large UDP DNS responses as fragments and dropping them. Two options: lower tunnel MTU to 1436 or enable EDNS0 response size clamp.
ankur: Also check for source NAT changes. If firewall started symmetric NAT, our ESP flow may be mapped to different ports and BGP/ISAKMP keepalives get confused.
support-esc: Customer confirmed they reverted the firewall policy that blocked ephemeral UDP and added NAT keepalive to 30s. They also applied MTU clamp to 1436 on the site-to-site device.
natalie: After those changes, BGP stabilized ~10:42 and our control-plane TLS handshake success rate jumped back to normal. DNS queries started succeeding.
maria.g: Customer reports API auth flows recovered and error rate dropped to baseline at 10:48. They left the firewall firmware in place but rolled back the restrictive policy.
ops-oncall: For permanent fix: recommend customer: - maintain ephemeral UDP allowlist for NAT-T - enable MSS clamping or set tunnel MTU 1436 - disable DF on their firewall for ESP fragments (or enable reassembly) - add our control-plane IPs to egress allowlist (TCP 443, UDP 500/4500) - increase NAT keepalive frequency if using symmetric NAT
jamie: We'll add monitoring alert to detect BGP holdtime drops and TLS handshake failure spikes for Private deployments in eu-west-1 tied to customer VIFs.
support-esc: Customer requested a formal RCA and a note to their network team about vendor firmware behavior. I'll draft and share. :white_check_mark:
maria.g: Thanks everyone. Follow-up ticket: NET-2026-554 to track vendor firmware compatibility guidance. Closing incident once RCA doc posted.
ops-oncall: Leaving note: temporary route failover to secondary DX path used during flap, no data lost, all sessions recovered. :thumbsup:
